q: How many unique people have contributed code to Valkey across all its releases?
explain: About 280 people have shipped code in a Valkey release, as of October 2026.

q: How many people have participated in valkey-io/valkey on GitHub by opening, commenting on, or reviewing an issue or PR?
explain: Around 950 people have opened, commented on, or reviewed an issue or PR in valkey-io/valkey, as of October 2026.

q: How many GitHub stars does valkey-io/valkey have?
explain: valkey-io/valkey sits at about 27,000 GitHub stars, as of October 2026.

q: Which is a real Valkey command?
explain: It pops from the right of one list and pushes to the left of another, blocking until there's something to pop. BLMOVE has since replaced it.

q: What does "PF" in PFADD stand for?
explain: PF is for Philippe Flajolet, who invented the HyperLogLog behind every PF command.

q: What was Valkey called before it was Valkey?
explain: At first the fork was literally called PlaceholderKV, because naming things is hard.

q: Which version did Valkey fork from?
explain: Valkey forked from Redis 7.2.4, the last BSD-licensed release.

q: Which is a real Valkey error?
explain: SCRIPT KILL or FUNCTION KILL returns NOTBUSY when no script is running.
LOLWUT is a joke command that prints a piece of computer-generated art along with the server version. Versions 5 and 6 came from Redis, and Madelyn added version 9 for Valkey.

q: How many characters long must a module data type name be?
explain: Nine characters at 6 bits each, plus a 10-bit encoding version, fit exactly in a 64-bit type ID in the RDB file.
